findings.title: Sensitive data broadcast without protection
findings.rationale: MainActivity sends a broadcast containing LoginData (email and password) with a custom action. Although the receiver is not exported, the broadcast is sent implicitly. Any app on the device can register a receiver for this action and intercept the credentials. The action name suggests it is unprotected.

findings.title: Arbitrary code execution via DexClassLoader
findings.rationale: OversecuredApplication loads and executes code from a file on the shared storage (/sdcard/updater.apk). Any app on the device can write a malicious APK to this location, leading to arbitrary code execution with the app's permissions.

findings.title: Cleartext HTTP traffic for login
findings.rationale: The Retrofit instance uses an HTTP base URL. Login credentials are sent over cleartext HTTP, making them vulnerable to interception by a network attacker (MITM).

findings.title: WebView allows file access from file URLs
findings.rationale: WebViewActivity enables JavaScript and allows file access from file URLs. If the WebView loads a malicious page (e.g., via the deeplink or intent redirection), it can read local files and exfiltrate sensitive data.

findings.title: Weak encryption with hardcoded key
findings.rationale: WeakCrypto uses AES with a hardcoded key and the default mode (likely ECB or CBC with a fixed IV). The key is visible in the decompiled code, allowing an attacker to decrypt any data encrypted with this class, such as the token sent to the WebView.

findings.title: FileProvider exposes entire filesystem
findings.rationale: The FileProvider configuration exposes the entire filesystem root. If the FileProvider is used to share files, an attacker could potentially access any file on the device by crafting a URI.

findings.title: Deeplink allows setting arbitrary login URL
findings.rationale: The deeplink handler allows setting the login URL to any value provided in the query parameter. An attacker can craft a deeplink to redirect the login process to a malicious server, capturing user credentials.

findings.title: Plugin loading from other packages
findings.rationale: OversecuredApplication loads and invokes code from other packages that start with 'oversecured.plugin.'. An attacker can install a malicious plugin app and have its code executed within the app's process, leading to privilege escalation or data theft.

findings.title: Log output contains sensitive data
findings.rationale: LoginActivity logs the LoginData object, which contains email and password, to the debug log. This information can be read by other apps with the READ_LOGS permission or by an attacker with access to the device.

findings.title: Credentials stored in plaintext SharedPreferences
findings.rationale: LoginUtils stores email and password in plaintext in SharedPreferences. Since the app is debuggable and allows backup, these credentials can be easily extracted by an attacker with access to the device or its backups.

findings.title: Debuggable build allows code injection and memory dump
findings.rationale: The application is marked as debuggable. This allows any app on the device to attach a debugger to the process, inject code, dump memory (exposing credentials in LoginUtils), and bypass security controls.

findings.title: Arbitrary file write via exported Service
findings.rationale: InsecureLoggerService is exported and accepts a file path from the intent extra. It writes logcat output to this path. An attacker can specify a path to overwrite critical system files or app data, leading to privilege escalation or data corruption.

findings.title: Arbitrary file read via exported ContentProvider
findings.evidence:
File file = new File(Environment.getExternalStorageDirectory(), uri.getLastPathSegment());
        return ParcelFileDescriptor.open(file, 805306368);
findings.rationale: TheftOverwriteProvider is exported and openFile constructs a file path using the last path segment of the URI without validation. An attacker can pass a URI with a path segment like "../../data/data/oversecured.ovaa/shared_prefs/login_data.xml" to read sensitive files on the device.

findings.title: Hardcoded credentials in resources
findings.rationale: The app contains hardcoded credentials (adm1n:passw0rd) in the strings resource. If this URL is used for any network request, the credentials are exposed to anyone who can decompile the app or access the resources.

findings.title: Intent Redirection in LoginActivity
findings.evidence:
Intent redirectIntent = (Intent) IntentCompat.getParcelableExtra(getIntent(), INTENT_REDIRECT_KEY, Intent.class);
        startActivity((Intent) LoginActivity$$ExternalSyntheticBackport0.m(redirectIntent, new Supplier() {
findings.rationale: LoginActivity is exported and reads a Parcelable Intent from the incoming intent. It then starts this intent directly. An attacker can craft an intent with a malicious redirect_intent to launch arbitrary activities or services with the app's identity, potentially bypassing authentication or accessing protected components.
